thread:
jules: saw repeated p99 spikes when a batch touched a prefix that was being demoted. seems like eviction and batching are stepping on each other. thoughts?

maria: yup, saw a similar incident this morning. two options: make eviction batch-aware or make coalescer avoid fragile prefixes.

kai: eviction-aware is safer for batching but couples eviction. coalescer-only is simpler but drops batching efficiency.

lee: could we combine: small hysteresis credits per-prefix to absorb churn + a lightweight batch-epoch tag for in-flight batches? credits prevent oscillation; epoch protects active batches.

nina: combo makes sense. credits handle frequent flips, epoch avoids mid-batch demotes. both ephemeral.

jules: implementation sketch: credits as u8 per-prefix, replenish token-bucket style; batch_epoch as u32 stamped by coalescer; eviction checks epoch map -> skip if active; otherwise apply credit check.

maria: testing plan: microbench with synthetic churn, e2e trace for mid-batch eviction, metrics: batch_epoch_conflicts, credit_deferrals, backend_miss_rate. default caps: credits=3, epoch_ttl=2s.

kai: rollout via runtime flag + canary 5% shards. ops-bot: schedule canary.

ops-bot: registered canary `infra/canary/evict-hyst-batch-probe` - 5% for 12h. capture specified metrics.

lee: will author short RFC addendum with fallbacks and knob names. reviewers: @maria @kai.

jules: thx — good incremental plan.
